To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The effect of photoreactivating UV light on the survival of Escherichia coli WP2s cells, carrying the R46 plasmid, was investigated.
The photoreactivation of UV‐inducible mutants in the mutator strain was reduced at low fluences of photoreactivating UV but increased at higher ones.
photoreactivating UV fluences below the threshold for the induction of the SOS response in Escherichia coli WP2s carrying the R46 plasmid, reduced the yield of mutants per 106 UV survivors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the photoreactivation effect of the mutagenic action of UV light in Escherichia coli WP2s carrying the R46 plasmid.
the effect of photoreactivating (PR) light on UV‐induced lethal and pre‐mutational DNA lesions in the WP2s E. coli strain.
the effects of UV radiation on the growth and survival of microorganisms and their genetic systems and with the mechanisms of UV‐induction and repair of DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the photoreactivating effect on mutagenesis is a consequence of the SOS‐repair of cyclobutane dimers, while the photoreactivation effect on lethality is a consequence of direct photolyase action on the cyclobutane photoproducts.
the plasmid‐dependent mutagenicity is not due to a general increase of the number of UV photoproducts, but rather to an increase in the proportion of pre‐mutational photoproducts.
the plasmid R46‐mediated mutagenicity is due to a combination of SOS and P‐repair.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
photoreactivation of UV damage is a complex phenomenon.
the plasmid R46 mutator system is a very efficient system to induce mutations by the P‐repair system, but it does not interfere with the SOS‐repair system of the bacterial cell.
the plasmid R46 is a mutator plasmids which is able to induce a SOS‐like error prone DNA repair mechanism in E. coli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that photoreactivation can be a powerful tool for the detection of UV photoproducts in DNA that are not detectable by conventional methods.
photoreactivation is a very useful tool for investigating the effects of light on DNA damage and repair.
the photoreactivation effect of light on the number of UV induced mutations is dependent on the fluence of the UV light used.
